question: A Site Bind, spike planted default, 2v2, 22s. You're KAY/O at A Short (2 flashes), teammate at CT. One ATK spotted A Long. What do you do?

options.label: Throw ZERO/point (suppression) onto site, then flash and coordinate the entry with your CT teammate onto the spike
options.explication_courte: ZERO/point strips the post-plant util (no molly or flash to delay the defuse) and the flash opens the entry; hitting from both axes (Short + CT) saturates a 2-man defense.

options.label: Blind-flash A Long and duel the isolated ATK to equalize at 1v1 before retaking the spike
options.explication_courte: Trading the spotted A Long ATK simplifies to 1v1, but burns clock on a tight timer (22s) and leaves the second ATK free on the spike during the duel.

sources_option.citation: Trading a known attacker can simplify the retake, but chasing a pick off-site costs clock the defenders often cannot afford on a short timer.

options.label: Hold CT with your teammate and time the retake for the last seconds (~8s) to minimize exposure
options.explication_courte: Retaking too late on a default plant leaves no margin: if one angle holds out, the timer runs before you clear the second ATK. Coordination is fine but the timing is too slow.

sources_option.citation: A defuse needs 7 seconds; retaking with under ~10 seconds left on a contested spike leaves no margin to clear a second holder before detonation.

options.label: Rush the spike solo through A Short without util to buy defuse time while your teammate rotates
options.explication_courte: A solo dry-peek into a spike held by 2 full-buy in crossfire is a free kill handed to the ATK; without a flash or suppression it's a 2v1 gift.

sources_option.citation: Solo dry entry into a held post-plant hands the attackers a free trade; util and coordinated timing are what break the crossfire, not raw aggression.

explication_longue:
Situation: 2v2 retake on A Site Bind, default plant, 22 seconds. You're KAY/O with ZERO/point (suppression), FRAG/ment (molly) and 1 FLASH/drive; your teammate is at CT; one ATK is spotted A Long, the second is unknown (likely on or near the spike or hookah).

The challenge of a 2v2 retake on default plant Bind is that both attackers hold a crossfire covering the spike from A Long and the back of site. Two principles apply: (1) strip the defenders' delay util so no molly hits you on the defuse, (2) push from two distinct axes so 2 defenders can't cover both of you.

KAY/O's strength here is ZERO/point: suppression disables any abilities on enemies caught in the zone, meaning no Viper/Brimstone molly or Phoenix flash to delay the defuse. Combine that with a flash entry and coordinated Short+CT push, and you turn a shaky 2v2 into a structured retake. Hunting the A Long pick is viable (acceptable option) but eats precious clock on an already tight timer.

Estimated elite distribution: ~52% play suppression+flash+coordinated entry, ~24% go for the A Long pick first, ~18% stall too long (risky late retake), ~4% solo rush without util (the mistake). GTO tolerance: any sequence that coordinates both players and neutralizes enemy util is acceptable; the solo dry-peek is the only real mistake.

sources.citation: Coordination matters most on the retaker side; a coordinated entry with utility clears angles faster than defenders holding a crossfire can react.
Use utility reactively and to deny the enemy's delay tools; suppressing or blinding the holders opens the window to plant/defuse contest.
A spike planted in the open forces ~2.4 extra seconds of exposure to defuse; combined with the 7s defuse, timing the retake before ~10s left is critical.

_gaps.incertitude: Le DEF est en semi-buy (KAY/O util complete supposee) ; si les armes sont plus faibles, l'equation duel A Long change et l'option 'chercher le pick' pourrait devenir couteuse.
Estimations depuis guides retake/post-plant ; l'usage precis de ZERO/point en retake 2v2 varie selon la composition adverse (agents a util de retard) non specifiee.
La position du 2e ATK est supposee sur/pres du spike mais non confirmee ; un juge Immortal+ pourrait ajuster la ligne optimale selon un stack A Long a 2 plutot qu'un split.
